children: The revised allowance structure increases HRA to 27% for X-category cities, 18% for Y-category cities and 9% for Z-category cities, following the VDA revision to 26.8%
Coal India has revised House Rent Allowance (HRA) rates for eligible non-executive employees across the company and its subsidiaries, increasing the housing benefit in all three city classifications.

The revised rates will apply retrospectively from September 1, 2026, following an increase in Variable Dearness Allowance (VDA) beyond the threshold prescribed under the 11th National Coal Wage Agreement (NCWA-XI).

An office order issued by Coal India's Human Resources department on October 22, 2026, confirmed the revised allowance structure. The change will benefit employees covered under the applicable wage-board provisions, with the revised HRA calculated as a percentage of basic pay.
Check Revised HRA Rates Across City Categories
Under the updated structure, employees posted in X-category cities will receive HRA equivalent to 27 per cent of basic pay, compared with the earlier rate of 24 per cent.

For Y-category locations, the allowance has been increased from 16 to 18 per cent of basic pay. Employees working in Z-category cities will now receive 9 per cent, against the previous rate of 8 per cent.

The revision translates into an increase of three percentage points for X-category cities, two percentage points for Y-category cities and one percentage point for Z-category cities.
The actual additional amount payable will depend on an employee's basic salary and the applicable classification of their posting location.
VDA Crosses 25 Per Cent Threshold, Triggers HRA Revision
The allowance enhancement follows the revision of VDA for wage-board employees to 26.8 per cent, effective September 1, 2026.
Under the provisions of NCWA-XI, an increase in VDA beyond the specified 25 per cent level triggers a corresponding revision in HRA rates.
With the latest VDA adjustment taking the figure to 26.8 per cent, Coal India has implemented the revised housing allowance structure in accordance with the applicable wage agreement.
The HRA will continue to be calculated on basic pay, subject to existing eligibility requirements and the company's rules governing allowance payments.
HRA Benefit To Extend Across Coal India Subsidiaries
The revised rates cover eligible non-executive employees of Coal India and its subsidiaries, subject to the conditions specified in the office order.

These include Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL), Central Coalfields Limited (CCL), Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL), Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL), South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), Western Coalfields Limited (WCL) and Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Limited (CMPDIL).

Since the revised structure takes effect from September 1, 2026, eligible employees will be entitled to the enhanced allowance from that date, subject to payroll processing and applicable company guidelines.

The decision increases the housing allowance component of compensation for Coal India's eligible non-executive workforce. The extent of the financial benefit will vary depending on individual basic pay and the city category in which employees are posted.
